What should I budget for carpet installation in Cottage Lake, WA?

Two numbers cover most of it. Installed, carpet runs $4 to $7 a square foot, and that rate carries the pad, the labor, new tack strip and hauling the old floor off. Most projects here land at $2,000 to $4,500; a 1,200 sq ft main level plus the stairs to a daylight basement is closer to $5,500 to $8,500. Grade decides where in those ranges you fall, and you judge grade with full-size samples lying on the floor they'd cover.
Does the mobile carpet showroom really come out to Cottage Lake?

Cottage Lake sits off the retail map, which is exactly the address this van was built for. What does carpet stretching cost near Cottage Lake?

Ripples usually show up first in the long hallways and daylight-basement rec rooms these houses are built around. Restretching in Cottage Lake starts at $99 per room. A power stretcher takes out waves, buckles and trip edges for roughly a fifth of replacement cost, so while the pile is healthy and the color still suits you, that's the cheaper answer.
What do carpeted stairs cost in a Cottage Lake home?

Stair work starts at $18 per step, whether you want a waterfall wrap or a tailored cap-and-band. Landings and pie-shaped winders get counted into the written quote at the measure, so the stair total you approve is the stair total you pay.
How long will carpet installation take at my place?

One day covers most Cottage Lake homes. Three or four rooms plus a staircase is a normal day's work; a large acreage house with a daylight basement, lots of stairs and heavy furniture can stretch into a second day. Your quote lists the schedule in writing, so you'll know before install day.
Will you move furniture, or do I empty the rooms first?

We move the big pieces — beds, dressers, sofas, tables — on most jobs and return them to their spots when the carpet is in. Your part is the small stuff: closet floors, electronics, breakables and anything personal you'd rather carry yourself.
How do I know whether to restretch my carpet or replace it?

Four things end a carpet's life: traffic lanes crushed flat, seams pulling apart, backing breaking down, or pet odor that survived professional cleaning. Any one of those, and stretching just delays it. None of them — pile still standing, backing sound, a color you can live with — and a $99-per-room stretch does the job instead of a new floor. Out on the acreage lots it's often one hard-used room gone and the rest merely loose. We look before we quote.

What carpet works best for pets on a Cottage Lake property?

Horse properties, muddy dogs and the occasional barn boot set the bar out here. What clears it: a moisture-barrier pad underneath, a sealed backing above that, and solution-dyed nylon on top. The first two stop accidents before they reach the subfloor, which is where odor turns permanent; the third takes a diluted-bleach scrub without losing color. Moving up to the barrier pad starts at $0.65 per square foot.
